_what: Everything this migration deferred, with a PROBE where one exists. `node scripts/cssMigrationCycle.mjs --worklist` prints these under the family lanes and re-measures each one, so an item cannot quietly stop being true. Add here rather than to a message: four of these were first recorded only in a commit body, which nothing re-reads.
_lanes: open = do it. blocked = waiting on a named thing. decided = examined and deliberately not done; kept so it is not re-raised.

items.what: 33 families, 114 rules, that NO bundle renders. Neither movable nor provably dead.
items.why: A visual diff cannot tell a dead class from one that only renders inside a dialogue the fixtures never open. Deleting on a diff alone is the one action in this migration the instrument cannot validate.
items.note: CLOSED 2026-09-09. PL-53 shipped and answered it: 254 rules deleted against its level-1 bar, and the last two survivors — .node-version-line and .section-label — went the same day, each probed by exact token with three positive controls at the same scope (intflow-section-label returns 1, which is what proves the probe is not matching substrings). The DEAD? lane is empty.

items.what: Comment blocks in custom-spectrum.css naming a departed family with NO rule beneath them.
items.why: The mover took the rule and left the comment for the first eight cycles. 74 were reunited on 2026-09-09 and the remaining 8 on the same day once the duplicate selectors blocking them were merged. One is left: a tombstone reading '.brand-card-check retired — replaced by the shared .selection-check-corner', which belongs next to its replacement rather than where the deleted rule used to be.
items.note: CLOSED 2026-09-09 at 0. Seven, not the one this row claimed — the probe was right and the prose was stale. Six were section headers in one 64-line stretch whose families had all left, and they hid two @keyframes that should have travelled with their rules: vsteplist-step-enter -> vstep-list.css and sum-check-in -> build-summary.css, each with exactly one user. A @keyframes resolves by NAME, so it must sit in a sheet the consuming bundle loads; verified in the built bundles that both now reach exactly the entries that use them (wizard+configure, wizard) instead of all eight. The .brand-card-check tombstone moved next to its replacement in shared-ui.css. `--orphans` now PRINTS the list, because a probe that returns only a number cannot be acted on and this one had been wrong four times.

items.what: Test suites that read a stylesheet BY PATH instead of using tests/helpers/cssRules.ts.
items.why: They assert on where a rule LIVES as much as on what it says, and this migration moves rules between sheets by design. Four suites have broken this way on moves that changed no rendering at all. Two more broke on the .page-* move on 2026-09-09 — pageContentAlignment and destinationRowType, each carrying its own copy of ruleFor — and were converted. That is six of the six that have ever broken; the rest either use the helper or read the sheet as data on purpose.
items.note: CLOSED 2026-09-09. The count of 13 was a grep for the FILENAME, which mostly caught comments recording an earlier conversion. Exactly one suite still read a sheet by path — ProjectCard.test.tsx — and it had gone VACUOUS: it opened custom-spectrum.css for `.project-card-spectrum-components`, which moved to project-cards.css on 2026-09-09, so indexOf returned -1, the slice produced '' and both assertions passed on an empty string. Converted to tests/helpers/cssRules.ts, which THROWS on a missing selector. Proved non-vacuous by planting flex-grow:1 and watching it fail. The other three hits are the legitimate ones this row already named.

items.what: A generated sheet header still carrying the placeholder instead of its entry list.
items.why: The mover writes the header BEFORE the imports are added, so it cannot know the entries. Reach is the property ADR-017 section 6 turns on and the one a reader cannot get from the file itself.
items.note: CLOSED 2026-09-09 at 0 — every generated sheet header names its entry list. The probe stays; it is how a new sheet with a placeholder header gets caught.

items.what: src/features/project-creation/ui/styles/integration-flow.css holds only `.int-*`, the results LIST. The Add Integration flow is `.intflow-*` and lives in add-integration-flow.css.
items.why: The name predates the split and is wider than the file's contents, which is exactly the kind of thing the next person reads as authoritative. A rename is cheap and touches one import.
items.note: CLOSED 2026-09-09 — renamed to integration-results.css. One import, plus cross-references in its own header and in add-integration-flow.css, which still described the .intflow-* family as living in custom-spectrum.css.

items.what: `.manage-apis-body .intflow-api-picker` is still in custom-spectrum.css after .intflow-* left.
items.why: It is a `.manage-*` rule that styles intflow elements as descendants, so it belongs to that family and moves when `.manage-*` does. Correct as it stands, recorded so it is not mistaken for an incomplete move.
items.note: CLOSED 2026-09-09, and it found a SHIPPED BUG rather than a leftover. The .manage-* rules had already left for shared-ui.css with the shared-ui batch, so this row was stale. What was still true is worse: `.manage-apis-body .intflow-api-picker,` sat on its own line with `@layer theme {` inserted BELOW it, splitting a comma-separated selector list with an at-rule. Chrome keeps ZERO rules from that shape — measured in a real browser against the correct form as a control (flex-grow 0 vs 1). Three sheets shipped it (shared-ui, data-installer, connect-services) and nothing caught it: esbuild injects CSS as a string and never parses it, and the visual baseline had captured the broken state as its own 'before'. All three fixed; a parse check with a planted control now lives in tests/sop/stylesheet-bundles.test.ts, and control R in the mover's --selftest pins that a multi-line selector list starts at its FIRST line.

items.what: Selectors declared twice in one sheet with no conditional copy — i.e. real duplication.
items.why: Nine were merged on 2026-09-09. SEVEN groups remain and every one is a base rule plus a copy inside @media or prefers-reduced-motion, which is how a breakpoint is written. An earlier count of five came from looking at only the sheets that cycle touched; index.css and connect-services.css hold one each. The probe excludes conditional groups, so it reads 0 and a real regression would show.
items.note: The seven legitimate overrides: .sidebar-tile-grid, .vsteplist-step, .choice-card and .choice-card:hover:not(:disabled) in custom-spectrum.css, .status-dot--pulse in index.css, .services-cards-grid in connect-services.css, .wizard-timeline-column in wizard-timeline.css.

items.what: Two comment blocks sat one blank line above a moved rule and stayed in the god file.
items.why: Attachment is deliberately ADJACENT-ONLY: a block one blank line up is as likely to be a section banner over several families, and taking it would move a heading away from most of what it heads. Two of 84 is the cost of that choice.

items.what: Flip the cascade per feature sheet (step 3), then sweep !important (step 4).
items.why: Step 3 is where the 762 moved elements arrive, in reviewable batches, and it needs the owner per surface. PL-33 is blocked on it too: its 'vendor CSS sits in the lowest cascade layer' convention cannot be enforced until it is true. Stopping after step 2 remains a legitimate destination.
items.blockedOn: step 4 only. Step 3 is UNDER WAY, one entry at a time.
items.note:
STEP 3 STARTED 2026-09-09 with the sidebar, at the owner's instruction to try it before the release rather than after. The build's CSS plugin is now a factory and the webview build is two contexts; `LAYERED_VENDOR_ENTRIES` in esbuild.config.js names which entries get Spectrum wrapped in @layer vendor, and tests/sop/stylesheet-bundles.test.ts pins both that list and the order string against the sheets. RESULT: ZERO of 276 elements moved — sidebar, 2 themes x 3 widths, 46 elements each. Controls: the vendor layer confirmed live in the captured document (16 blocks, 20 order declarations, the CSSOM parses the statement); a width comparison on the same data reported 4 changes; a tampered value was detected. NOT MEASURED: interaction states. 8 hover/focus rules reach this bundle, and capture-interactions.js threw its forcing control — identically on the UNLAYERED control build, so the instrument is at fault and not the change. That gap is written up in the webview-visual-baseline skill. NEXT ENTRY: pick the next smallest and repeat; step 4 (the !important sweep, 1,309) stays blocked until enough entries are layered that removing one cannot promote a Spectrum rule on an unlayered surface.

PROJECTSLIST TRIED AND REVERTED 2026-09-09, the same day. 45 of 77 elements moved per cell, and TWO OF THE CHANGES ARE VISIBLE, not sub-pixel: INPUT line-height 32px -> 21px and BUTTON font-weight 700 -> 400. Property counts in one cell: line-height 36, width 17, font-weight 4, height 2. That is the SAME SIGNATURE as the whole-repo attempt of 2026-09-08, which also named input line-height and buttons losing their bold — so per-surface scoping does not avoid the problem, it localises it. 

WHAT THE TWO SURFACES SAY TOGETHER. The sidebar moved ZERO and projectsList moved 58%, and the difference is not size — it is that the sidebar renders almost no Spectrum FORM controls. Sidebar: 3 sheets, 114 rules, 1 input. projectsList: 6 sheets, 235 rules, and its Spectrum ActionButtons and TextField are exactly where the vendor demotion bites. So the entries left to do are not a queue to grind through in size order; the cheap ones are the ones with no Spectrum form controls, and every other entry will reproduce projectsList. 

NOT DIAGNOSED: which declaration wins once Spectrum is demoted. A CSSOM probe for rules matching the input found none, which would mean the value is inherited rather than set — but that probe has no positive control and should not be believed as it stands. Whoever picks this up should establish that first: it decides whether step 3 needs OUR sheets changed, or is simply wrong for surfaces with Spectrum form controls.

items.what: `.section-label` sits in src/core/ui/styles/step-scaffold.css and no feature or shared component uses it.
items.why: Found by the ADR-017 §7 enforcer on 2026-09-09, which skips zero-user classes rather than reporting them as misplaced — placement and deadness are different defects. It belongs with the 33 dead families, but it is now in a core sheet rather than the god file, so a sweep of the god file alone will miss it.
